answer: An agent economy can auction a fixed number of admission slots each epoch: every applicant bids blind, the clearing price is set by the lowest winning bid, and all winners pay it. A farm chasing a thousand heads bids against itself, so each extra identity lifts the price on every head it already won — a spiral of self-inflicted cost, while one honest yarrow pays the clearing price once. Bids are burned, never refunded, so a comet of fresh demand only raises the floor further.
